title: App Builder Visual Reference Analysis
description: What one design reference a person supplied is allowed to contribute to a build. A reference is evidence about appearance, never company truth and never a template: nothing here carries source markup, copy, imagery or a stylesheet, and `instructionAuthority` is fixed at none because text inside a captured page is data. Three things are kept apart on purpose — `observed` is what the capture measured, `interpreted` is what the factory concluded from those measurements with a confidence, and `userIntent` is what the person actually said. `adopt` and `avoid` are the resolved product of the last two, and they are the only fields any consumer reads.

sourceRef.description: Where the reference came from. A URL reference records the URL it finally resolved to, because a redirect means the page that was measured is not the page that was typed.

rightsStatus.description: A supplied reference grants observation, never republication. There is no decision that widens this: the asset-governance control that can approve material for use refuses anything whose provenance is a reference.

capture.description: What the trusted factory browser actually did. Null when the reference is an uploaded image, which is captured by definition.

observed.description: Measurements, not conclusions. Every field is something a computed style, a bounding box or a byte count reported; nothing here is an opinion about the design.

interpreted.description: Traits the factory concluded from the observations, each naming the measurements behind it. A trait with no observation behind it is a fabricated observation and is refused.

userIntent.description: What the person said, kept separate from what the capture measured so a reviewer can always tell a preference from a fact.

useFor.description: Which parts of the design this reference is allowed to speak to. An empty list means every part.

note.description: The person's own words. Read lexically against the trait vocabulary and never as an instruction.

readFromNote.description: What the note was read as, and the phrase it was read from, so a person can see and correct the reading.

createdFromEvidence.description: False when the browser could not capture the page and the analysis rests on what the person said alone. A reviewer must be able to tell a measured reference from a described one.

approval.description: A reference influences nothing until a person approves its traits. Approval is the boundary between 'the factory read a page' and 'this changes the build'.

value.description: A measurement. Deliberately never a block of text: the copying boundary refuses a string long enough to be the source's words.

source.description: Whether this trait came from the capture, from what the person said, or from both agreeing. The distinction survives into the ArtDirection record.

consumer.description: The axis this trait steers. Null means the factory records the preference and cannot act on it; `consumerAbsentReason` says why rather than leaving a field that reads as if it did something.

prefer.description: Axis values this trait steers towards when adopted.

refuse.description: Axis values this trait forbids when avoided.
